answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, with transition mass attenuated at each step and weighted by verified stake. A Sybil cluster creates a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits escape probability, while min-cut transitivity bounds the trust mass it can import from honest regions and hence its aggregate voting weight. At dawn, even a river of colluding identities finds no haven against spectral expansion.
